chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who has penalties due upon him, one of which is killing, he said: The penalties are established upon him, then he is killed.

key_terms.الْحُدُودُ: Penalties (specifically hudud, fixed punishments in Islamic law)

ai.seo_question: What is the order of executing multiple penalties when one is death in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the judicial sequence for a person bearing multiple *hudud* penalties, ruling that they are executed sequentially rather than simultaneously, with death serving as the final penalty. This establishes the principle of cumulative execution in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring each legal obligation is fulfilled before the individual's life is taken. The ruling underscores the precision of Islamic penal law in handling complex cases of multiple offenses.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who happens to have (several) Penalties due upon him, from these is the killing. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The (other) Penalties would be established (first), then he would be killed’.
